data.narrative:
Lumaril is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Mark Elliot and Ben Duffield that has raised $12M to date. The comparable universe consists of nine private robotics and manufacturing companies and one public peer (277810.KQ), including competitors such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method given data constraints. Using the $12M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $30M. Peer-median analysis is not applicable; while ten same-sector peers exist, the dataset contains insufficient narrow peers (fewer than three) at identical or adjacent stages with comparable valuation tiers to support a reliable median benchmark without introducing misleading distortion from all-sector aggregation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with a median point of $30M. This range reflects the single applicable method and carries meaningful uncertainty. Key risks include reliance on a single quantitative approach and the absence of narrowly comparable contemporaneous transactions. Any valuation within the $26M–$34M band is defensible on current data; movement outside this range would require additional comparable transaction evidence or material operational performance updates since the $12M raise.
